item.title: Beyond AI infrastructure, India’s tech boom rests on the efficient use of power and water
item.description: At TechSparks 2026, founders of SolarSquare and Boson Whitewater unpack why overcoming perception, pricing gaps, and consumer trust matters far more in climatetech than just building the technology.
item.content:encoded:
India’s technology conversation is increasingly dominated by artificial intelligence, data centres and digital infrastructure, however a more fundamental challenge lies in ensuring that the country has sufficient reliable power and water to sustain its growing cities and industries.

At TechSparks 2026 in a panel discussion titled The Invisible Infrastructure: Rebuilding India’s Energy, Water and Clean Air Systems, Shreya Mishra, Co-founder and CEO of SolarSquare, and Vikas Brahmawar, Founder and Director of Boson Whitewater discussed on how on the significance of scaling these solutions which require more than technological innovation. 

Rooftop solar moves beyond a niche market

The residential solar market in India has undergone a significant transformation over the past five years, said Shreya Mishra, Co-founder and CEO of SolarSquare. 

Recalling the market, she said that when SolarSquare entered the market, adoption was limited, consumers had little understanding of rooftop solar, and the upfront investment made many households hesitant. The company, however, believed that the economics of distributed power generation and the need for energy security would eventually drive adoption.

“Distributed solar, which is solar on every rooftop, will be the cheapest source of power,” Mishra said.

According to Mishra, it took five years for one lakh homes in India to adopt residential solar when the company began its journey. Today, the country adds that many homes in a single week, so far SolarSquare has powered more than 60,000 homes. 

However, the economics alone do not eliminate consumer concerns. Rooftop solar requires a substantial upfront payment, and households may worry about equipment reliability, maintenance costs and whether the system will generate the promised amount of electricity.

For companies in the sector, building trust is therefore as important as making the financial case. Mishra also sees distributed solar as a way to reduce the cost associated with transmitting electricity over long distances. While power may be generated relatively cheaply, transmission and distribution costs can increase the price consumers ultimately pay.

Her argument is that generating electricity closer to where it is consumed can help address that gap. 

SolarSquare currently serves both individual households and around 500 housing societies. 

Wastewater as an alternative to freshwater

On the other hand, water presents a different challenge. Vikas Brahmawar, who moved from the software industry to work on water reuse, said it took years of effort to build the policy environment needed to support the sector.

“Water, unlike solar, there is a fixed sun which is hitting,” he said, explaining that wastewater treatment must account for changing water quality. The business also needs supportive policies and viable economics to scale.

The need is becoming more pressing as cities and industries compete for increasingly constrained freshwater resources. Groundwater extraction remains a major source of supply, while industrial applications such as data centres, cooling towers, semiconductor manufacturing, electroplating and laundry require significant quantities of water.

Brahmawar said the company had repurposed around 147 crore litres of water over the preceding four years that would otherwise have gone down the drain.

The opportunity is particularly relevant as data centres expand and demand for water-intensive infrastructure rises. Reusing treated wastewater for industrial purposes could help ease pressure on freshwater sources while creating a commercially viable market for recycled water.

But the economics of water supply can be counterintuitive. Brahmawar pointed to Bengaluru’s Cauvery water supply, saying consumers are charged around Rs 7 per kilolitre even though the government spends about Rs 95 per kilolitre to bring the water from a distant river to the city.

The gap, he suggested, illustrates the challenge facing alternative water sources: a solution must compete not only with the availability of freshwater but also with the way existing water systems are priced and subsidised.

Technology is not the biggest hurdle

If rooftop solar has benefited from increasingly visible consumer savings, recycled water faces an additional barrier: public perception.

Brahmawar recounted how the company spent two-and-a-half years speaking to more than 300 apartment complexes about the possibility of using recycled water, including for drinking. The response showed that convincing people to accept treated wastewater can be difficult even when treatment technology is available.

For now, the company is concentrating on industrial applications, where recycled water can replace freshwater without requiring consumers to overcome the same psychological barrier associated with drinking it.

“Technology is the least of the problem,” he said. The bigger obstacles, in his view, are commercial viability, public perception, enforcement and execution on the ground.

Building a broader energy ecosystem

SolarSquare, meanwhile, is looking beyond the installation of rooftop panels. Mishra said the company wants to become a full-stack home energy brand, expanding into batteries, electric-vehicle chargers, home energy monitoring, energy optimisation and smart-grid integration.

The company is also using software to monitor installations and identify problems remotely. Mishra said monitoring data could help detect voltage fluctuations and recurring power outages, allowing the company to identify potential issues and recommend solutions such as battery storage where appropriate.

Such capabilities can improve customer service while reducing the need for physical inspections, she said.

The experiences of SolarSquare and Boson Whitewater highlight two different stages in the development of climate infrastructure. Rooftop solar is benefiting from growing consumer awareness and a clearer financial proposition, while wastewater reuse is still working to overcome pricing, policy and perception barriers.

However, the common challenge for both the companies lies in how to turn a technically viable solution into infrastructure that people and organisations can adopt at scale.

item.title: Info Edge reports steady business growth ahead of leadership transition
item.description: Revenue from operations grew 12% YoY, while net profit was up 87%. Growth was driven by recruitment business, 99acres, and matchmaking services.
item.content:encoded:
Info Edge (India), which owns and operates internet-led businesses, delivered steady business growth in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026. Consolidated revenue from operations rose 12.2% year on year (YoY) to Rs 903.9 crore, while profit after tax was up 87% YoY at Rs 649.8 crore.

Growth was supported by the recruitment business, faster expansion at property portal 99acres, and continued momentum in the matchmaking business. However, the education segment remained under pressure.

Profitability improved as expenses grew more slowly than revenue, although higher other income also contributed to the increase in reported profits.

There is also a leadership transition in the offing. Hitesh Oberoi is due to leave the full-time role of Managing Director and CEO on December 2 this year, after nearly 27 years with the company. Founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani is slated to assume an expanded executive role from December 3, subject to shareholder approval.

Operating growth improves

Info Edge operates the brands Naukri (online recruitment), 99acres (property listings), Jeevansathi and Aisle (matchmaking), and Shiksha (education services). It also invests in other businesses. So its financial results reflect both operating performance and changes in investment values.

Consolidated total income, including other income, increased 37.7% YoY to Rs 1,332.3 crore. Other income rose 164.8% to Rs 428.4 crore from Rs 161.8 crore, while total expenses increased 4.5% to Rs 588.6 crore from Rs 563.5 crore. Profit before tax, before exceptional items, rose 85.2% to Rs 747.7 crore.

Consolidated PAT reached Rs 649.8 crore, up 87% YoY from Rs 347.5 crore. This includes profits attributable to non-controlling interests in subsidiaries. The portion attributable to Info Edge’s shareholders was Rs 479.7 crore, up 51.6% from Rs 316.4 crore.

Based on consolidated revenue, expenses, depreciation and finance costs, operating EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) comes at approximately Rs 354 crore, up 27.4% YoY, with a margin of 39.2%, compared with 34.5% a year earlier. 

Standalone revenue from operations rose 12.8% to Rs 841.7 crore, while operating profit before tax increased 29.8% to Rs 347.3 crore. Its margin expanded to 41.3% from approximately 35.9%.

Standalone PAT, however, fell 92.9% to Rs 333.8 crore from Rs 4,720 crore. The previous year’s quarter included an exceptional gain of Rs 5,200 crore arising from an unrealised investment valuation gain following the amalgamation of Makesense Technologies with PB Fintech. The decline therefore does not represent a comparable deterioration in operating performance.

Revenue streams diverge

Recruitment remained the largest revenue contributor. The company's earnings presentation, which includes acquired businesses in its operating-business breakdown, puts recruitment revenue at approximately Rs 682 crore, or 75.4% of the total. Standalone recruitment revenue grew 13.3% YoY to Rs 632 crore, while operating profit before tax increased 19.9% to Rs 374 crore. Its operating margin reached 59.1%.

Recruitment billings grew 12.6% in Q2 and 14.9% in the first half of FY27. Candidate Services billings increased 37%, while AI and data products for recruiters and job seekers accounted for a high single-digit share of recruitment topline.

Real estate contributed approximately Rs 134 crore, or 14.8% of revenue. 99acres revenue grew 16.7% YoY, while billings increased 21.2%. Property enquiries rose over 33% and app daily active users grew 25%. Operating losses narrowed 93% to Rs 1.6 crore, while cash from operations rose to Rs 22 crore from Rs 2.3 crore. These figures indicate improving business economics, although sustained operating profitability remains a test.

Matchmaking contributed around Rs 53 crore, comprising Rs 40 crore from Jeevansathi and Rs 13 crore from Aisle. Jeevansathi revenue grew 16.5% and it reported operating profit of Rs 2 crore. Aisle revenue increased 35.1% and billings rose 40%, but it recorded an operating loss of Rs 3 crore. Combined matchmaking billings grew 23.1% YoY.

Education remained the weakest business. Shiksha generated approximately Rs 35 crore in revenue, down 8.5% YoY, while billings fell 27.2%. The company attributed the pressure to AI-related traffic headwinds, declining Google-referred search traffic and subdued student interest in studying in the US, with preferences shifting towards the UK, Australia and Europe. The business reported negative operating cash flow of Rs 16 crore. 

Cash and transition

Standalone cash generated from operations before tax rose 27.4% YoY to Rs 372.8 crore. The company reported a cash balance of approximately Rs 4,976 crore as at September 30, 2026, including balances held by wholly owned subsidiaries.

The company board has declared an interim dividend of Rs 3 per share and approved an investment of approximately Rs 150 crore in wholly owned subsidiary Redstart Labs. It has also approved exits from the stakes in Medcords and Unnati Online, investments that had been fully impaired in earlier years.

Edited by Swetha Kannan

item.title: Ace Blend bags $9.91M as it looks to scale science-led nutrition
item.description: The nutrition company will use the funding to advance research-led product development and launch patented nutrition formats.
item.content:encoded:
Ace Blend, a science-led nutrition company, has raised $9.91 million in a Series A2 funding round led by 3one4 Capital, a venture capital firm whose portfolio includes Licious, Darwinbox and Kapiva.

Existing investor Fireside Ventures, an early-stage investor in consumer brands, has increased its backing after leading Ace Blend’s $3.3 million pre-Series A round.

The new funds will support research-led product development and the commercial launch of patented nutrition formats, with the first expected in the fourth quarter of FY27.

Founded in 2018 following more than a decade of research, Ace Blend develops supplements targeting heart health, immunity, sleep, recovery and brain health.

Co-founder Saif Mehkri joined in 2022, bringing nearly three decades of experience in the nutrition industry.

The company said its approach starts with clinical evidence, using research to determine a nutrient’s form, dose and delivery rather than building products around popular ingredients. It also controls sourcing, formulation and manufacturing, while clinical validation and automated testing are conducted by accredited laboratories in Europe.

Partnerships with ingredient suppliers DSM and TCI give it exclusive rights in India to certain technologies, according to the company.

Ace Blend claims 300% growth in FY26, with more than 46% of its customers returning to purchase.

Fireside Ventures principal Ankita Balotia cited repeat purchases and word of mouth as evidence of consumer trust. However, repeat buying alone does not independently establish a supplement’s clinical effectiveness.

3one4 Capital managing partner Pranav Pai said the company was “tackling the hardest problems in nutrition”, including developing formulations suited to Indian needs and maintaining consistent quality.

The funding comes amid wider investment activity in Indian nutrition. TruNativ raised $30 million in June, led by healthcare investment firm OrbiMed. In July, daily supplement brand Supply6 secured Rs 48 crore from Unilever Ventures and Zeropearl VC. More recently, The Stack raised Rs 21.5 crore in October to expand research and its product portfolio.

These investments point to growing investor interest in differentiated formulations, product innovation and repeat demand in a crowded market.

Regulation remains important as brands make increasingly specific health claims. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has regulations covering health supplements and nutraceuticals, alongside separate rules governing advertising and claims.

In February, the government said there was no dedicated Ministry of Food Processing Industries scheme for nutraceuticals, although broader food-processing programmes support infrastructure development.

item.title: India’s new-age manufacturers to benefit from $3 trillion global AI investment cycle: Avendus Capital
item.description: The investment banking firm has identified defence and aerospace, space technology, robotics and automation, semiconductors, energy transition, and advanced materials as the sectors that will drive India’s next phase of industrial growth.
item.content:encoded:
India’s new-age manufacturing sector could benefit significantly from a $3 trillion global AI infrastructure investment cycle, according to a report by Avendus Capital.

The investment banking firm has identified defence and aerospace, space technology, robotics and automation, semiconductors, energy transition, and advanced materials as the sectors poised to drive India’s next phase of industrial growth, offering key opportunities for domestic companies.

The report highlighted 2027–28 as a critical period for commercialisation as companies move from policy support and project approvals towards production.

The opportunity is being driven by rising global investments in AI infrastructure, increasing demand for energy infrastructure, and growing geopolitical security concerns. India’s domestic demand, engineering talent and policy framework could help manufacturers reduce import dependence and build globally competitive capabilities.

“India's new-age manufacturing opportunity is substantial, but its right-to-win manifests in select segments,” said Koushik Bhattacharyya, Managing Director and Head of Industrials Investment Banking at Avendus Capital.

With more than 80% of the $3 trillion AI infrastructure investment yet to be deployed globally, India has an opportunity to capitalise on its domestic demand base, engineering capabilities, and policy support, he said.

Semiconductors and space technology are among the segments showing significant growth potential. India’s semiconductor consumption is projected to more than double from $49.5 billion in 2025 to $106.5 billion by 2030, creating opportunities in chip design, packaging, testing, and specialised materials.

India’s space economy is expected to expand more than threefold, from approximately $13 billion in 2025 to $44 billion by 2033. Domestic defence production is projected to reach around $31.6 billion by 2030, while the robotics market could grow nearly fourfold to $4.6 billion by 2030, supported by wider adoption and import substitution.

The report also expects India’s clean-energy manufacturing ecosystem to move further upstream over the next five years. By the end of the decade, the country could establish an integrated solar manufacturing chain spanning ingots to modules, several gigawatt-hour-scale battery cell plants, and commercial production of indigenous electrolyser stacks and rare-earth-free motor technology.

Advanced materials represent another emerging opportunity, with rising domestic demand and heavy import dependence creating scope for local capacity building. Recycling is expected to scale first, followed by battery materials, while rare-earth magnet manufacturing could advance with policy support.

The coming years will test India’s ability to translate these opportunities into commercially viable manufacturing capabilities, the report said.

item.title: Meesho narrows loss by 68% while revenue rises 34% in Q2 of FY27
item.description: The annual transacting user base of Meesho now stands at 284 million for Meesho and the seller base has grown to 1.13 million.
item.content:encoded:
Ecommerce company Meesho reported a 68% decline in net losses even as revenues rose by 34% on a year-on-year (YoY) basis for the second quarter of FY27.

Meesho reported a net loss of Rs 132.44 crore for the three months ending September, 2026 which is the second quarter of FY27 as compared to Rs 411.36 crore recorded in the similar period a year ago.

Revenue for the second quarter touched Rs 4131.58 crore as compared to Rs 3073.67 crore a year ago.

On the performance of the company, Meesho CEO Vidit Aatrey said, “Our Q2 performance reflects the strength of Meesho's operating model, with NMV (net merchandise value) growing 23% year-on-year to Rs 12,911 crore and annual transacting users reaching 284 million. More consumers are shopping on Meesho, and they are shopping more frequently, even as first-time buyers grew 16% quarter-on-quarter.”

According to the company, annual transacting users grew 21% YoY to 284 million while annual purchase frequency increased 7% YoY to 10.4 transactions per user. Meesho said NMV grew 23% YoY.

Meesho said festive-aligned NMV grew 33% YoY over the 90 days preceding Dussehra. The annual transacting sellers increased 60% YoY to 1.13 million. The e-commerce company said over 4 lakh sellers are now part of its Content Commerce ecosystem, enabling entrepreneurs to reach consumers through creator-led product discovery.

For Meesho, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a big differentiator as it transitions towards an agent-led software development with engineering productivity increasing 171% between March and September 2026 and the number of experiments rising 73%.

It noted that approximately 65% of engineering pods now operate with a single engineer directing AI agents.

“Our focus remains on reinvesting these efficiency gains into better consumer and seller experiences, accelerating innovation and building a larger, more efficient marketplace that can generate sustainable free cash flow over the long term,” Aatrey said.

Meesho said as of September 30, 2026, it had a cash balance of Rs 7,048 crore, providing flexibility to pursue long-term growth opportunities while maintaining financial discipline.

item.title: CloudSEK launches incubation programme for cybersecurity startups
item.description: Launchpad is a 12-week programme offering mentorship, investor connections, threat intelligence resources, and access to potential customers and channel partners.
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based AI-powered cybersecurity and threat intelligence company CloudSEK has launched CloudSEK Launchpad, a 12-week incubation programme for early-stage cybersecurity startups.

The first cohort will have 10 companies, each eligible for up to $5,000 in AI model credits. Applications are open until November 20, 2026.

According to a statement, the programme is built around product development and commercial adoption rather than mentorship alone. Selected founders will get weekly guidance from CloudSEK’s leadership on research, product, enterprise sales, and fundraising, along with access to its threat intelligence resources and researchers. CloudSEK will also introduce founders to potential customers and channel partners across India, the Gulf Cooperation Council region, and the United States.

The programme ends with a demo day where founders will pitch to investors and prospective customers.

Pre-seed and seed-stage startups can apply; so can idea-stage founders with a strong team and a clearly defined security problem. Areas of interest include security for AI systems and agents, AI-native security operations, threat intelligence, identity and fraud prevention, and software supply-chain security.

Rahul Sasi, Founder and CEO of CloudSEK, said, “When we started CloudSEK, I wished someone had shown us the shortcuts, which customers to call first, which mistakes cost a year and who to trust.

"AI has made it significantly easier to build sophisticated technology, but building a successful cybersecurity company still requires access to real threat intelligence, trusted customers and the right industry network. With Launchpad, we want to share what we have learned and help promising founders get to their first ten paying customers."

Alongside Launchpad, CloudSEK has also introduced KeyVigil, a secure gateway that lets applications and autonomous AI agents access frontier AI models through a single endpoint. It manages master API keys centrally, masks sensitive data before it reaches a model, and flags and blocks prompt-injection and jailbreak attempts. It also logs model interactions and lets organisations set spending limits for teams, applications and agents. KeyVigil is available to enterprise customers, and Launchpad participants will receive access to it through their credits.

item.title: IG Defence, Oman’s MSA Global explore production of drone systems
item.description: India’s IG Defence and Oman’s MSA Global have signed an exploratory MoU to explore co-development and local manufacture of drone and counter-drone systems for Oman and the wider Gulf.
item.content:encoded:
India’s IG Defence and Oman-based MSA Global have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to explore the co-development and local manufacture of drone and counter-drone systems for Oman and the wider Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC).

The agreement links India’s defence-export ambitions with Gulf security concerns, but remains exploratory and does not confirm an order, factory or deployment.

Reuters reported in October that Iran and allied groups had carried out at least 135 drone and missile attacks against 84 infrastructure sites across Gulf Arab states since the United States and Israel began bombing Iran in February.

“The evolving security environment in the Gulf reinforces the importance of strengthening indigenous defence capabilities and developing resilient regional manufacturing ecosystems,” MSA Global chairman Col M. S. Atwal (Retd.) said.

The MoU was exchanged during the India-Oman Defence Industry Cooperation Seminar in Muscat in October. India and Oman already have established defence ties, including joint exercises involving all three branches of India’s armed forces.

IG Defence, formerly known as IG Drones, said discussions will cover three systems. KAL is described by the company as a one-way attack unmanned aerial system with a stated range of up to 1,000 kilometres. BAJ is an unmanned aerial interceptor intended for counter-unmanned aircraft system (C-UAS) use, while JWALA is a micro-missile system under development for counter-drone applications.

“Our partnership with MSA Global reflects our vision of taking India's indigenous defence technologies to global markets through strategic industrial collaboration,” IG Defence Chief Executive Officer Bodhisattwa Sanghapriya said.

The agreement comes as India’s defence exports reached Rs 23,622 crore in the 2024-25 financial year, up 12.04% from the previous year. On October 26, India also approved in principle Rs 2,12,000 crore in military acquisitions, including counter-drone systems and long-range attack drones.

Other companies are responding to similar demand. In May, France’s CS Group won a NATO contract to supply two counter-drone systems for its Brussels headquarters. In August, US firm Powerus announced a separate contract for counter-drone technology to protect Middle Eastern energy infrastructure.

item.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 29, 2026)
item.description: YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, October 29, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Artificial intelligence poses numerous challenges for employees but can improve governance in governments, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.

Featured stories

Vembu’s AI warning: one worker could do the work of ten

Artificial intelligence (AI) could allow one skilled employee to do work that previously required 10, reshaping employment even as it creates new opportunities. That is the warning from Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu. “What it does mean is a rebalancing across the economy and that is painful when we go through it. The only thing we can do is to accept that it is coming and be prepared for it,” he wrote on X.

Read more

Maharashtra launches MahaINDUS AI to speed up government work

Maharashtra is giving its government offices an AI upgrade. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis launched MahaINDUS, an AI platform designed for government offices, on October 28, 2026. The government said the initiative aims to improve transparency, accountability and administrative efficiency. By combining AI with integrated databases, departments are expected to find eligible beneficiaries, verify claims and assess welfare schemes more effectively.

Read more

Beyond AI infrastructure, India’s tech boom rests on the efficient use of power and water

At TechSparks 2026, founders of SolarSquare and Boson Whitewater unpack why overcoming perception, pricing gaps, and consumer trust matters far more in climatetech than just building the technology.

Read more

Funding news

Venttup raises $3M co-led by Rainmatter and Unicorn India Ventures

Industries 5.0 startup Venttup has raised $3 million in a pre-Series A funding round co-led by Rainmatter, backed by Zerodha, and Unicorn India Ventures. The company will use the funds to expand its engineering team, establish precision manufacturing capabilities and invest in rapid prototyping and AI-led sourcing.

Venttup is setting up a manufacturing facility in Bengaluru to support precision machining, turning and sheet metal production for energy transition, defence, aerospace and space applications. The company reported fivefold growth to ₹10 crore in FY2025-26 and has added over 15 blue-chip customers in the past year. Its business opportunity pipeline stands at approximately ₹30 crore.

Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre raises Rs 28 crore in Series A

Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre has raised Rs 28 crore in its first institutional funding round, led by Alkemi Growth Capital. The investment will support geographical expansion, increased clinical capacity, specialised care programmes and stronger insurance and corporate partnerships.

Founded in Pune in 2008, Jagruti provides mental healthcare, addiction treatment, rehabilitation and elder care services. The organisation currently operates more than 19 centres across nine cities, with over 1,600 beds and 40 doctors. It has supported more than 82,000 individuals. Jagruti plans to expand to over 40 centres and 4,000 beds across Tier I and Tier II cities over the next three to four years.

Coratia Technologies raises Rs 18 crore for underwater robotics

Underwater robotics startup Coratia Technologies has raised Rs 18 crore in a bridge funding round led by MGF Kavachh. The capital will support execution of its Rs 66 crore Indian Navy contract under the iDEX initiative, research and development, product development and manufacturing expansion.

Founded by Debendra Pradhan and Biswajit Swain, Coratia develops indigenous underwater robotic systems for defence, infrastructure and industrial applications. Its flagship Jalasimha underwater remotely operated vehicle has achieved Technology Readiness Level 9. The company's technologies can also support inspections of dams, bridges, ports, pipelines and offshore assets. Coratia had raised Rs 17 crore from MGF Kavachh, Piper and SIDBI in a pre-Series A round in 2025.

Carbelim secures Rs 10 crore from IIT Madras Unicorn Frontier Fund

Kerala-based deep-tech startup Carbelim has secured Rs 10 crore from the IIT Madras Unicorn Frontier Fund, becoming the first startup from the state to receive investment from the fund. Founded by Karthika Gopi and Rahul Babu, the company develops microalgae-based carbon capture and air-purification systems that absorb atmospheric carbon dioxide and convert it into oxygen. Carbelim has filed 13 patents, including seven in the US and six in India.

The funding is expected to help the company create more than 50 jobs and pursue its target of achieving Rs 100 crore in turnover through international markets. The Rs 1,000 crore fund is backed by IIT Madras, IIT Madras Research Park and Unicorn India Ventures.

Docterz raises Rs 5 crore, with doctors contributing 60% of funding

Healthcare technology company Docterz has raised Rs 5 crore from approximately 35 investors, including doctors who use its platform. Nearly 60% of the funding came from around 20 doctors, alongside investors such as SUGAR Cosmetics co-founder Vineeta Singh and former CaratLane CEO Avnish Anand. Founded by practising paediatrician Atish Laddad, Docterz provides digital medical records, appointment management, billing and patient engagement tools.

Its platform supports more than 5,000 doctors across India, with a strong presence in paediatrics. The company will use the capital to expand its reach, explore acquisitions and develop practical AI-enabled tools for medical practitioners, while maintaining a focus on patient data security and clinical independence.

ISLAND Beauty raises Rs 2.58 crore from AJ VC

Skincare brand ISLAND Beauty has raised Rs 2.58 crore from AJ VC to support product development, brand awareness and customer acquisition. Co-founded by Shirley Setia, Korean skincare expert Jinsoon Lee, Mayank Jain and Sakshi Jain, the company combines Korean skincare ingredients with formulations developed in India for local weather conditions and consumer needs. Its proprietary Core Barrier Matrix approach focuses on both skin-barrier repair and defence, encouraging simpler and more consistent skincare routines.

The brand's current portfolio includes cleansers, toners, serums, moisturisers and lip-care products. Over the next three years, ISLAND Beauty plans to expand its product range and strengthen its market presence, positioning itself around barrier-focused skincare for Indian consumers.

Viridian Ingni Propulsion raises Rs 1.47 crore in pre-seed round

Chennai-based propulsion technology startup Viridian Ingni Propulsion has raised ₹1.47 crore in a pre-seed round led by Inflection Point Ventures. The company has also secured ₹53.75 lakh in grants from government programmes and other institutions. Founded in February 2024 by Sriram G, the startup develops electric propulsion systems integrating motors, controllers and firmware. The funding will help it move from validated prototypes to pilot production, establish manufacturing infrastructure and complete certification requirements.

Other news

Dialog Axiata, IITM Pravartak partner on technology research

Sri Lankan connectivity provider Dialog Axiata has partnered with IITM Pravartak Technologies Foundation to advance applied research and technology development in Sri Lanka. The memorandum of understanding, signed in Colombo, will connect research networks with Sri Lankan universities, government bodies and industry stakeholders.

The collaboration will explore innovation and incubation, applied research, artificial intelligence, skills development and international knowledge sharing. Initial areas under consideration include Sinhala and Tamil conversational AI, technology-enabled dengue prevention and solutions to human-elephant conflict. The partnership will begin with selected pilot projects before considering wider deployment. The initiative aims to strengthen Sri Lanka's research capabilities and translate academic work into practical solutions addressing national and societal challenges.

Zoho upgrades Analytics with agentic AI capabilities

Chennai-based technology company Zoho has upgraded Zoho Analytics with an intelligence layer designed to connect business data, contextual understanding and automated actions. The platform introduces semantic and ontology layers to help AI agents interpret organisational structures, business terminology and key metrics. Its conversational business intelligence assistant, Ask Zia, uses six specialised sub-agents to handle data analysis, modelling, visualisation, preparation, coding and SQL generation. The platform also supports automated workflows, more than 500 existing data connectors and 30 additional connectors.

New governance features allow administrators to monitor agent activity, data access and costs. Zoho Analytics also introduces enhanced visualisations, forecasting tools and data science capabilities, enabling businesses to move from reporting towards AI-assisted operational execution.

Urban households expected to spend Rs 1.97 lakh crore this festive season: Local Circles

Urban Indian households are projected to spend approximately ₹1.97 lakh crore on festive purchases in 2026, according to a LocalCircles study. The estimate is around ₹12,000 crore higher than in 2024, despite moderating from the previous year's GST-related high. About 57% of urban households plan festive purchases, spending an average of nearly ₹20,000 each. Clothing, footwear and accessories lead planned purchases, followed by home appliances, furniture and travel. The study also points to growing demand for quick commerce as consumers postpone purchases until closer to festivals. Platforms including Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart, Zepto, Amazon Now and Flipkart Minutes are expanding their reach and reporting higher festive-season activity.

Fruugo partners with PayGlocal to help Indian sellers reach global markets

Global online marketplace Fruugo is entering India through a partnership with cross-border payments company PayGlocal and technology and operations provider DMSMatrix. The initiative will give PayGlocal's more than 12,000 merchants access to Fruugo's international marketplace, helping Indian businesses sell to consumers across more than 40 countries. Sellers in categories including electronics, clothing and home decor will be able to explore overseas demand and diversify their sales channels. The partnership combines Fruugo's international shopper network with PayGlocal's payments infrastructure and DMSMatrix's onboarding and operational capabilities. The initiative targets micro, small and medium enterprises seeking greater product visibility as domestic e-commerce competition intensifies and international online shopping continues to expand.

upGrad School of Technology partners with MongoDB

upGrad School of Technology has partnered with MongoDB to strengthen industry-integrated engineering education and prepare students for modern software development and AI applications. The collaboration will provide eligible students with access to MongoDB for Academia, technical learning resources and fully sponsored certification vouchers. The two organisations will also explore curriculum enhancements, hackathons, innovation challenges, guest lectures, internships and career opportunities. Faculty members will receive access to technical resources, while designated faculty champions will support adoption of modern database technologies.

The partnership aims to bridge the gap between academic learning and industry requirements, particularly in cloud-native development, artificial intelligence and database engineering. It will give students practical exposure and recognised credentials to improve career readiness.

Procol's AI procurement platform manages over $30 billion in spending

AI-powered procurement technology company Procol is helping manufacturing enterprises automate purchasing workflows across multiple plants, suppliers and business units. The company works with more than 150 manufacturing businesses across over 10 countries, including Havells, Emami, Blue Star and Aditya Birla Group. Its platform automates processes spanning supplier onboarding, requests for quotations, electronic auctions, approvals and accounts payable, while integrating with enterprise systems such as SAP and Oracle. Procol says its implementations have saved buyers more than 8,100 hours of manual work and enabled procurement cycles to become significantly faster. The company currently manages over $30 billion in spending and reports generating more than $1 billion in savings across its customer base.

Wadhwani FPO Entrepreneurship Program launched in Karnataka

The Centre of Excellence for Farmer Producer Organizations, supported by Karnataka's Department of Horticulture and the National Entrepreneurship Network, has launched the Wadhwani FPO Entrepreneurship Program in the state. The initiative aims to strengthen Farmer Producer Organizations through business planning, market access, mentoring and execution support.

Its first Growth Bootcamp brought together 27 FPOs and more than 60 participants, including government officials, business experts and FPO leaders.

Participating organisations assessed their businesses, identified growth opportunities and selected priority initiatives for the next 12 months. They will now enter a structured 10-week programme featuring expert-led group and individual sessions. The programme aims to help FPOs become more sustainable enterprises, improve farmer incomes and create rural economic opportunities.

Devnagri AI expands from translation to multilingual AI infrastructure

Language technology company Devnagri AI has announced an evolution from a translation-focused platform to multilingual AI infrastructure for enterprises. The company aims to integrate language capabilities directly into business workflows rather than treating translation as a standalone function. Its offerings include multilingual content processing and AI-driven communication tools designed for customer-facing services and internal operations.

The platform supports cloud, hybrid and on-premises deployment, enabling organisations to integrate language technology within their existing security and technology environments.

Founded in 2021 by Nakul Kundra and Himanshu Sharma, Devnagri AI focuses on helping businesses engage users in their preferred languages. The company believes contextual multilingual capabilities will be increasingly important as enterprises expand AI adoption across India's linguistically diverse markets.

TutorCloud AI launches integrated platform for K-12 education

TutorCloud AI has launched an integrated artificial intelligence-powered platform connecting students, teachers, parents and school administrators in one ecosystem. Designed for K-12 education, the platform aims to support personalised tutoring while giving educators and families greater visibility into students' learning journeys.

The initiative reflects a focus on using AI to help teachers understand learning progress and identify student needs, rather than simply generating answers. By bringing different stakeholders onto a common platform, TutorCloud AI seeks to improve coordination between classroom instruction, home support and school administration.

The company positions the system as a way to make learning more personalised and connected, while enabling educators to use technology to better understand and support individual students.

Wissen Technology strengthens Singapore leadership with Tinku Gupta

Wissen Technology is strengthening its Singapore operations through a delivery-led strategy focused on engineering expertise, product development and business outcomes. The technology services company has appointed Tinku Gupta as Vice Chairman of Wissen Technology Singapore. Gupta brings more than 30 years of experience spanning technology, financial market infrastructure, business operations and cybersecurity. Wissen aims to help enterprises modernise technology platforms and accelerate innovation.

Founded in 2000, the company says it has delivered projects worth more than $1 billion and serves over 20 Fortune 500 companies.

Vaani AI Research launches self-service platform for voice AI agents

Bengaluru- and Singapore-based Vaani AI Research has launched a self-service developer platform for building, deploying and managing voice AI agents. Users can describe the agent they want, preview its voice, configure actions and deploy it across phone calls, websites, applications and WhatsApp.

The platform is built around Vaani's voice infrastructure, which connects speech models with the systems needed to operate agents in production. Its capabilities include inference optimisation, memory and conversational controls.

The launch follows the company's experience deploying voice AI in enterprise workflows, where poor conversational experiences can frustrate customers and lead to lost opportunities. The platform aims to simplify development and deployment of voice-based AI services for businesses and developers.

Festive invoice financing crosses Rs 20,000 crore, says M1xchange

India's pre-festive financing volumes crossed Rs 20,000 crore in 2026, with micro, small and medium enterprises increasingly using formal invoice discounting to fund seasonal demand, according to trade receivables platform M1xchange. Financing for micro-MSMEs grew more than 100% year-on-year, while average daily festive financing increased over 40%. The company projects overall festive-season financing to grow approximately 30% this year.

Invoice discounting enables suppliers to access working capital against unpaid invoices, helping them purchase inventory and meet delivery commitments before customers make payments.

Sector-wise trends show strong festive-period activity in consumer durables, e-retail, e-commerce and paints. The findings highlight the growing role of formal credit mechanisms in supporting smaller suppliers during peak business periods.

Fluke begins local manufacturing of digital multimeter components in India

Fluke Corporation has launched a local manufacturing initiative in India, marking a step towards expanding its domestic manufacturing capabilities under the government's Make in India programme. The first phase covers manufacturing associated with the Fluke 115 and Fluke 117 digital multimeters, including local production of printed circuit board assemblies. The initiative follows the company's progression from Class II to Class I Local Supplier status.

Fluke said the move would strengthen its engagement with Indian customers and support the country's industrial development. The company aims to build local capabilities while maintaining its global standards for quality, precision and reliability. The initiative is intended to establish a foundation for further expansion of manufacturing operations in India.

Otto launches voice AI CRM for field sales teams

Voice AI company Otto, also known as Ottoverse, has launched a voice-based customer relationship management platform designed for field sales representatives. The system enables sales teams to manage CRM activities through phone calls rather than manually entering information after customer meetings. Representatives can report meeting outcomes, while Otto updates deal records, saves contacts, drafts follow-up emails, creates tasks and prepares summaries for managers.

The platform uses voice AI models trained on field sales conversations and is designed to recognise product names, part numbers and different accents. Its context layer connects calls, meetings, emails, calendars and enterprise resource planning records to provide relevant customer information. Headquartered in New York and Mumbai, Otto is backed by Gutter Capital.

Masai School cuts course fees by 50% in IIT Patna partnership

Masai School has reduced course fees by 50% across its programmes through a partnership with Vishlesan i-Hub at IIT Patna, aiming to make technology upskilling more accessible. The programmes include Analytics with Agentic AI and Applied AI and Machine Learning Essentials, with the latter also available in Tamil and Telugu.

About 70% of Masai's students come from Tier II and III cities. The collaboration will combine industry-led mentoring, access to the IIT ecosystem and placement support. Vishlesan i-Hub has enrolled 14,971 learners across its programmes, with nearly 60% studying in languages other than English. The initiative seeks to address affordability and language barriers affecting access to employment-oriented technology education.

Hoopr launches Smash Plus for music licensing in TV and OTT advertising

Music technology startup Hoopr has launched Hoopr Smash Plus, a platform for licensing music for television commercials, OTT advertising, films, web series and corporate productions. Kisna Jewellers is the first brand to use the service, licensing the track 'Woh Kisna Hai' from the Tips catalogue for a campaign featuring Shahid Kapoor and Mira Rajput Kapoor. The platform aims to simplify macro-sync licensing, which typically requires separate agreements with record labels, publishers and copyright societies.

Indian corporates drive flexible office demand as BFSI is fastest-growing sector: myHQ

India’s flexible office market is entering a more mature phase, with Indian corporates and banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) companies driving demand, according to a report by myHQ. Indian corporates accounted for 23.4% of flexible workspace demand in 2026, up from 21.9% in 2025, becoming the second-largest company segment after startups. Their average requirement increased from 25 seats in 2023 to 55 seats in 2026.

BFSI’s share of demand rose 2.7 times to 12.2% from 4.5% in 2023, making it the second-largest industry contributor. IT/ITeS remained the largest segment at 43.9%, while startups accounted for 39.2% of demand.

HomeLane turns EBITDA positive in Q4 FY26; targets Rs 1,000 crore revenue in FY27

HomeLane, a technology-enabled home interiors company, reported a return to growth following the integration of its businesses, with revenue increasing 19% and its order book expanding 37% year-on-year in the first half of FY27. The company turned operating EBITDA positive in the fourth quarter of FY26, reporting quarterly revenue of Rs 212 crore and an operating EBITDA margin of 5%.

HomeLane expects to cross Rs 1,000 crore in revenue in FY27 and remain EBITDA positive for the full financial year. The company said its growing order book provides visibility into the second half, as projects typically convert into revenue over six to nine months. For FY26, revenue remained steady at Rs 745 crore as HomeLane prioritised integrating DesignCafe. Direct project costs declined to 52% of revenue from 56.6% in FY25.

Sorry Sugar launches zero-added-sugar Diwali campaign

Zero-added-sugar beverage brand Sorry Sugar has launched its Diwali campaign, ‘Yeh Diwali, Bina Cheeni Wali’, featuring a music-driven film that challenges conventional perceptions of festive indulgence and healthy consumption.

The campaign seeks to position healthier choices as an alternative to traditional sugary treats without compromising on taste or celebration. It will be rolled out across the brand’s digital channels.

The company has also introduced an Assorted Coffee Gift Set featuring zero-added-sugar flavoured coffee premixes, a reusable organiser box and a complimentary frother. Founded in 2026, Sorry Sugar sells its products through its website and leading direct-to-consumer and quick-commerce platforms.

item.title: Freshworks acquires Israel-based AI startup Robusta Dev
item.description: Freshworks said that this acquisition will strengthen Freshservice's capabilities, which is Freshworks’ IT service management platform, in incident management and IT operations.
item.content:encoded:
SaaS major Freshworks has acquired Israel-based AI startup Robusta Dev, an incident intelligence engine that uses AI to investigate technology disruptions, identify root causes, and recommend remediation actions.

In a company blogpost, Freshworks said that this acquisition will strengthen Freshservice's capabilities, which is Freshworks’ IT service management platform, in incident management and IT operations. It bridges the gap between deep diagnostic intelligence, IT service management, and modern incident orchestration. 

Nasdaq-listed Freshworks did not disclose the financial details of the deal.

Founded by Natan Yellin and Arik Alon, Robusta has been heavily optimised for large scale production environments. For many of its customers, even momentary reliability issues can cause a loss of revenue. Yet operating AI Agents at that scale is challenging because of the volume of alerts and the complexity of their systems. Robusta's technology allows customers use frontier intelligence to investigate their alerts, no matter the volume.

"LLMs are fantastic at troubleshooting incidents," said Natan Yellin, co-founder and CEO of Robusta. 

"Our technology lets AI Agents do that effectively in large enterprise environments, where there are so many raw events that investigating each one individually would be exorbitant from a token cost perspective. We're incredibly excited to join Freshworks, which gives us the scale and platform to bring that experience to engineering teams everywhere, while keeping humans firmly in control of decisions that touch production."

item.title: AI that speaks, codes and takes action: Inside Google Cloud’s Gemini masterclass
item.description: Why make AI do the talking when it can do the work too? At TechSparks 2026, Google Cloud’s Rajesh Shivani showed how Gemini agents can talk, code and crunch data.
item.content:encoded:
Imagine handing AI 80,000 files and getting back a presentation with charts, images and a clear narrative. Or asking it to build a detailed 3D scene using code, without dedicated rendering software. These are examples of AI moving beyond answering prompts to taking on complex tasks.

At TechSparks 2026, Rajesh Shivani, Head of AI Customer Engineering for Digital Natives, Startups and ITES at Google Cloud, demonstrated how Gemini is being used across voice AI, autonomous agents and software development.

His masterclass explored how businesses can move from using AI for answers to delegating work to it.

From chatbots to autonomous coworkers

AI tools initially gained traction through chat interfaces that answered questions. The next stage is agentic AI, where systems can plan tasks, access information, and use tools to act on a user’s behalf.

“An agent is nothing now but a model plus a harness,” Rajesh said, describing the infrastructure around a model that manages memory, context, permissions and task execution.

Building useful agents requires four elements: a goal, clear instructions, relevant knowledge and tools to act on that knowledge. A company’s internal data is particularly important because general-purpose models may not have access to its specific processes or customer information.

Shivani also discussed Google’s Open Knowledge Format (OKF), which aims to give organisations a structured way to make information accessible to AI agents.

Voice AI takes on real-world tasks

Voice was one of the key demonstrations. A system developed for Singapore-based Grab helped passengers and drivers coordinate airport pickups despite language barriers. The demo highlighted how voice AI could support interactions across more than 85 languages.

Another example showed AI dubbing an English video into Marathi and Malayalam while matching lip movements and facial expressions. Such capabilities could help businesses produce multilingual training material, marketing videos and customer communications with fewer production steps.

“Voice is becoming the new user interface,” Rajesh Shivani stated, pointing to the growing role of voice-based interactions for customers and employees.

He also showcased a virtual banking assistant created for Citibank’s retail banking experience. In the demonstration, the AI avatar explained options for a maturing certificate of deposit and submitted a renewal after the customer selected a 12-month term.

AI that builds, checks and creates

Beyond voice, Shivani highlighted Google’s tools for coding and cybersecurity. Antigravity helps developers build applications, while CodeMender can identify code vulnerabilities, generate patches and test them in a sandbox.

In one demonstration, Gemini analysed 80,000 files from NASA’s open archives, including Mars weather readings and helicopter telemetry, and produced a presentation using a supplied template and design guidelines.

Another demo showed a model generating a detailed 3D library scene using Python and NumPy, without dedicated rendering software or external assets.

For businesses weighing the cost of AI adoption, Shivani stressed that the most powerful model is not always necessary. “You don’t need to have a frontier model for everything,” he said, explaining why simpler tasks can use faster, lower-cost models.

Preparing businesses for AI agents

As agents take on more work, businesses will need to rethink how their systems handle permissions, security, costs and automated activity. Shivani urged organisations to consider a future in which agents, not just people, interact with their systems.

Developers, he suggested, could increasingly become managers of agents rather than handling every step themselves.

The challenge is no longer simply choosing a capable AI model. It is giving agents the right knowledge and tools, while ensuring they can complete tasks reliably and safely.

item.title: Bengaluru-based Inkle acquires Finally’s bookkeeping arm, expands team to 160
item.description: Bengaluru-built, San Francisco-headquartered CPA firm Inkle has acquired Finally's bookkeeping division in an undisclosed all-cash deal, taking its team to about 160 people across five countries and extending it from startups to non-tech small businesses.
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco-headquartered Inkle, an AI-driven accounting and bookkeeping firm for US companies that develops its technology in Bengaluru, has purchased the bookkeeping arm of small-business finance platform Finally. The price has not been revealed. Inkle describes the deal as an all-cash asset purchase and says it is the company’s first acquisition.

Around 100 Finally employees based in the Dominican Republic, Colombia, Puerto Rico, Miami, Boca Raton and New York will join Inkle’s 60-member team in Bengaluru, comprising engineers, product designers, tax professionals and bookkeepers. With a workforce of about 160 across five countries, Inkle says it can provide round-the-clock support to clients across the Americas and Asia. Finally’s existing bookkeeping customers will continue working with their current teams, while accessing services through Inkle’s software.

The acquisition also changes who Inkle works for. Until now, the firm’s clients have been mainly venture-backed startups. Finally’s customers are largely non-tech small businesses, including contractors, clinics, restaurants, professional services firms and owner-operators, a group Inkle regards as the core of America’s employer base.

“Ranvir and I are delighted to announce Inkle’s first acquisition,” said Anand Krishna, co-founder and CEO of Inkle. “Inkle is an American company that serves American small businesses, and it’s built in Bengaluru. That combination is our edge: U.S. CPAs who own the outcome, and an engineering team in India building the software and AI that let them serve far more businesses, far better, than a traditional firm. We’re building the AI-powered Big Four, and this acquisition helps us take that to the businesses that make up most of the American economy.”

Inkle cites a shortage of accounting professionals in the US as a factor behind the deal, with many CPAs and bookkeepers nearing retirement and fewer new entrants joining the profession. The AICPA’s 2025 Trends Report recorded 55,152 accounting degrees awarded in 2023-24, down 6.6% from the previous year. Inkle expects technology-led platforms to play a role in addressing the talent gap, with Indian engineers and finance professionals contributing to their development.

The company was set up in 2022 by Krishna, who runs it from San Francisco, and Ranvir Singh, who oversees technology from Bengaluru. It combines a US-licensed CPA practice with product, engineering and AI development carried out in India. The Bengaluru team built both Inkle Books, the firm’s general ledger, and its tax and compliance platform. Because developers work next to the accountants who use their tools, Inkle says problems flagged by the delivery side are frequently resolved within a day. It sees moving Finally’s team onto this platform as the most demanding test of that approach so far.

Inkle is also a frequent first stop for Indian founders looking to expand internationally. Each year it helps hundreds of businesses incorporate in the US, many of them Delaware C-Corps formed to raise investment and win American customers. It then looks after their continuing obligations, from federal tax returns and Delaware franchise tax to cross-border filings such as Form 5472 and FBAR. It is also the cross-border compliance partner for Stripe Atlas for Indian founders.

On funding, Inkle says it has become profitable after raising only $1.5 million in pre-seed capital from Picus Capital, Saison Capital and Force Ventures. That is well below what competing firms have raised, and several of those better-funded rivals have since exited the market. Inkle’s software costs nothing to use, and the company charges only for its AI-assisted bookkeeping, tax and compliance services. These can be delivered on Inkle Books, QuickBooks, Xero, Zoho Books or Mercury Books.
